headline: Tesla is reportedly expecting to build more than 1,000 Optimus humanoid robots a week by the end of 2026.
score_reason: Stays at pool 6: the target is a company expectation; the hand problem comes from one report.
importance_line: What changed: Tesla is aiming to raise output of its humanoid robot about tenfold, which matters to factory workers and to future buyers; the doubt: the 1,000-a-week goal is an expectation, the hand-assembly problem comes from a single report, and no sale price or date is set.
summary: BGR reports, citing an exclusive from The Information, that the hands and forearms of Tesla's Optimus humanoid robot need a lot of manual assembly, which slows production. BGR also reports that Tesla expects to make more than 1,000 Optimus robots a week by the end of 2026, and Elon Musk, Tesla's chief executive, has said the public could buy one by late 2027.
notes: Read in full. The article says Optimus robots are reportedly already working in Tesla factories; that is a claim, not shown, so machine_action is false (the story is about production targets).
